abstract: Exploring gene expression datasets often involves delineating principal axes of variation corresponding to either biological or technical variables. Principal component analysis (PCA) is typically employed as it uses all genes, reflecting global relationships between samples. Existing tools decompose gene expression first and interpret components afterwards. However, gene-level components are sensitive to sparsity and difficult to relate directly to biology, signals carried by low-variance components are easily overlooked, and differential pathway analysis is usually performed separately, on thresholded gene lists. PathwayTheme addresses these limitations by reversing the order of operations: per-sample pathway scores are generated first and then decomposed by PCA, so that each component is defined by pathways and can be tested directly against biological and technical variables. PathwayTheme further incorporates a statistical framework for supervised differential pathway enrichment that does not require thresholded gene lists, with Gene Ontology results summarised into themes. Applied to a published paediatric cancer cohort, PathwayTheme separated technical from biological axes and identified components distinguishing sample types, diagnoses and genetic subgroups, including rare groups represented by low-variance components.
